extracted.intended_audience: public-relations students and practitioners (press-release writers, agency and corporate communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for writing pickup‑worthy press releases within a broader strategic-writing/campaign context; covers planning, genre/format choice, drafting recipes, legal/ethical checks, multimedia integration, and evaluation. Intended as classroom and professional practice rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: State the goal of the release, the target audience, and the message before drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic step: define what you want the release to accomplish and for whom up front; this directs format, channel, tone, and evaluation. Marsh emphasizes articulating strategy prior to writing to avoid scattered or unfocused releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the receiving journalists' beats, deadlines, formats, and prior coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze target media and journalists to tailor content, angle, timing, and contact method. Knowing beats and deadlines helps choose lead info, appropriate depth, and whether to pitch or distribute on a wire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose distribution channel (wire, direct email, embargo, social-first) based on audience analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the channel that best reaches the intended audience and fits the news: wire services, targeted emails to reporters, embargoed briefings, or social-first releases. Channel choice affects timing, formatting, and follow-up tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide the appropriate document form (standard release, announcement, backgrounder, media advisory, statement, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the genre that fits the communicative purpose — e.g., media advisory for invitations, fact sheet for quick context, backgrounder for depth — rather than forcing a press release to perform other functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply genre conventions (lead, quote, inverted pyramid, boilerplate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Marsh's recipe conventions: include a strong lead, supporting factual paragraphs in inverted-pyramid order, at least one attributable quote, clear attribution, and a boilerplate. Particular ingredients (lead, quote, attribution, contact) are expected and should appear in conventional positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity & inclusion check
rubrics_metrics.description: Does language avoid stereotypes, exclusionary framing, single-perspective dominance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit wording, spokespeople, and format for inclusive language, representation, and accessibility. Use diverse spokespeople and accessible formats; quality outlets penalize releases that fail D&I expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the release pass PRSA Code compliance, accuracy, transparency?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review for honesty, full disclosure of conflicts, accuracy of facts and claims, and adherence to professional codes (e.g., PRSA). Ethics review should be an explicit step before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal review
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for libel risk, securities-disclosure obligations (if material), copyright, trademark, and FTC endorsement rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen for legal exposure: avoid defamatory statements, ensure necessary securities/regulatory disclosures if information is material, confirm rights to use media, and ensure endorsements/claims meet FTC standards. Consult counsel when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation plan
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide how success will be measured up front (clip count, sentiment, reach, engagement, downstream actions) so that distribution and calls to action align with measurable objectives. Marsh insists evaluation planning precede release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic-purpose statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A pickup-worthy release reflects a clearly articulated strategic purpose; releases lacking this read as scattered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state (for planning/grading) the release's strategic purpose: what it seeks to accomplish, for which audience, and what the key message is. Lack of a clear purpose is a common reason releases fail to get pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipe adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Marsh's recipe approach is explicit: certain ingredients (lead, quote, attribution, contact) must be present in fixed positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate releases for presence and conventional placement of required elements. Missing or misplaced ingredients (e.g., no contact, absent quote, weak lead) are grading faults and reduce pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document-type fit
rubrics_metrics.description: A misclassified release (e.g., press release used where a media advisory was appropriate) underperforms; choose the genre appropriate to the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the chosen document form matches the news function. Misuse of a press release to invite, to brief, or to argue reduces clarity and media pickup; select the correct tool for the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity & inclusion auditing
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusive language, diverse spokespeople, accessible format. Quality outlets penalize releases that fail this dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond wording, ensure representation among quoted sources/spokespeople and accessibility of assets (alt text, captions). This is treated as a discrete grading criterion in Marsh's rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics-and-legal checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Each release should be reviewed against ethical and legal flags before distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine ethics and legal checks into an explicit pre-distribution checklist covering PRSA compliance, factual accuracy, libel risk, securities disclosure, intellectual-property permissions, and FTC endorsement/commercial-speech rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Marsh insists on planned evaluation. The release writer should know how success will be measured (clip count, sentiment, reach, downstream action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable targets and methods for tracking results as part of the assignment/rubric; releases without evaluation plans fail the accountability dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic writing in the 2020s requires multimedia versions: social cards, video alt-version, podcast pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multimedia assets and repurposed versions for social and digital channels (images, social text, short video/audio bites). Evaluate whether the release package includes appropriate assets and platform adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-document consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: A release should be consistent with the issuer's other documents (annual report, social posts, executive bios) to avoid contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check facts, names, positions, tone, and claims for consistency with organizational messaging and other materials. Contradictions reduce credibility and are penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document-type ecology
rubrics_metrics.description: A release is one of many tools. A pickup-worthy campaign uses the appropriate document for each task: media advisory for invitation, fact sheet for context, backgrounder for depth, op-ed for argument, briefing memo for decision-makers, social post for retail reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate assignments in context of the campaign: was the correct mix of documents used? Penalize efforts that expect a single release to fulfill multiple distinct communicative functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is a function of appropriate document selection plus correct execution within the chosen genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marsh's pedagogy emphasizes that missing steps in the nine-step process — especially absent strategy, audience analysis, and ethics/legal review — compound to lower pickup rates and downstream credibility. Grading should reflect both selection and execution.
